messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Major: p99 latency breach detected for customer ACME (VPC: acme-vpc-eu-west-1). Metric: p99=4.2s (SLO=2.0s) over last 5m. Affected: dedicated pool acme-dedicated-eu-west-1. Paging @infra-oncall and @sara huang.

sara huang: ack — I'm on it. pulling dashboard now. link: https://console.redwood/investigate/alerts/1769004567

infra-oncall: acked. picking up initial triage. any customer-facing error spikes?

incident-bot: Error rate for ACME remains low (~0.3%). Token generation latency high. No auth errors. Backpressure observed on pool while queue depth rose.

mike oneil: data point from metrics: kernel queue length on cluster host g4-102 jumped ~3x at 10:14z. KV cache miss rate for ACME increased from 6% -> 42% around the same time.

jen choi: likely a cache eviction storm or sudden traffic pattern (longer sequences/options). Did anyone push model or config changes to that pool?

sara huang: no config deploys in last 24h for acme pool. ACME team reported a batch migration at 10:00z — check with acct-eng.

liam (acct-eng): reaching out to ACME support (dave) now — will confirm if they changed runtime prompts or started a job. dave, are you seeing anything on your side?

Dave (ACME): hey, yep we kicked off a large dataset re-indexing job hitting embeddings endpoints from eu-west region. Thought it would go to shared pool, but looks like VPC routing still sending it to our dedicated pool. We're pausing the job now.

mike oneil: that explains spike. dedicated pool got overloaded by high concurrency embeddings requests (long sequences). p95 climbed first then p99. need region-level mitigation while we clear storm.

jen choi: mitigation options: 1) throttle ACME inside control plane 2) failover tenant to their backup dedicated pool in eu-west-2 3) scale up acme pool replicas temporarily 4) apply routing to send long-seq routes to cheaper/quantized model variant. Thoughts?

infra-oncall: order of ops: quick open fix: route new requests to backup pool (eu-west-2) to stop p99 bleed. Secondary: scale up primary pool to drain backlog then bring routing back. Also add temporary per-tenant concurrency limit.

sara huang: agreed. I'm going to update routing policy and add a per-tenant throttle. mike, can you run the failover step? I'll prepare the commands and comms.

mike oneil: running failover now. Command:
```
redwoodctl routing set --tenant acme --from-pool acme-dedicated-eu-west-1 --to-pool acme-dedicated-eu-west-2 --strategy gradual --canary 10%
```
Applying canary 10% to validate behavior. I'll watch logs.

(2m later)

mike oneil: canary looks clean. p99 for canary requests ~ 1.6s. bumping to 50%.

jen choi: while canary expands, apply per-tenant concurrency cap to stop new long-tail jobs from overwhelming both pools.

sara huang: adding throttle:
```
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant acme --concurrency-limit 60
```
Throttle applied. Also enabling short-term cache warming: prewarm prefix caches for most common ACME prompts.

(3m later)

mike oneil: canary at 50% stable. Increasing to 100% now.

incident-bot: routing swap to acme-dedicated-eu-west-2 completed at 10:27z. Queue depth on primary dropped 40% within 2m. p99 observed falling from 4.2s -> 1.9s for routed traffic.

Dave (ACME): thanks — we paused the job. We'll spin it up against shared embedding pool after confirming quotas. Sorry about that.

liam (acct-eng): I'm pinging ACME's SRE and account team with status and ETA for full recovery.

jen choi: next step: scale down or resync primary pool when backlog drained. Also run postmortem item: tenant routing rules should respect explicit job target (shared vs dedicated).

sara huang: I'll hold handoff to follow-up owner. my shift ends in 18m — mike, can you take post-incident ownership and follow up with the PM/infra?

mike oneil: taking ownership. I'll monitor for 30m, then coordinate rollback of throttle and routing once ACME confirms job moved. Also will run `redwoodctl allocation scale --pool acme-dedicated-eu-west-1 --replicas 6` to help drain if queue persists.

(20m later)

mike oneil: p99 stable at ~1.8s across both pools. Concurrency cap lowered to 100 (incremental). Backlog drained to <5% of peak.

incident-bot: customer-impact note created: ACME experienced elevated latencies from 10:12z—10:32z affecting p99 (SLO breach). No increased error rates. Incident severity: Major.

liam (acct-eng): sent ACME incident update and next steps. They asked for a retro and configuration guardrails. I'll schedule a postmortem call tomorrow.

Dave (ACME): appreciate the fast response. Please include steps to prevent routing mistakes — this was due to our job mis-targeting. We'll add a safeguard on our side as well.

mike oneil: recorded runbook items: 1) add per-tenant long-sequence detection + routing policy 2) auto-throttle for sudden concurrency spikes 3) account-level alerting for large dataset jobs targeting dedicated pools 4) doc update for on-call failover commands.

sara huang: thanks team. handing off — mike, I left notes in incident doc. :thumbsup:

mike oneil: thanks Sara. I'll close after 1h of stability and a follow-up with ACME. Leaving the thread for postmortem notes.

jen choi: +1. Good run.

incident-bot: Incident closed to active mitigation at 11:02z. Postmortem assigned: infra-ml@redwood. Follow-up reminder scheduled for 24h.
